source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A frontal lobe brain tumor most likely causes:
questions.rationale: Frontal lobe tumors cause personality disturbances and inappropriate affect; temporal tumors cause olfactory hallucinations.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Intracranial tumors (PDF p. 360)
questions.quote: Personality disturbances • Inappropriate affect

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After craniotomy, the nurse notes yellowish drainage on the head dressing. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Yellowish drainage on a head dressing may be CSF and must be reported immediately.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Craniotomy care (PDF p. 360)
questions.quote: Report immediately to the physician, yellowish drainage on the head dressing. This indicates CSF leakage.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After craniotomy, a sudden large rise in urine output suggests:
questions.rationale: Pressure on the posterior pituitary can cause DI; monitor intake and output closely.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Craniotomy care (PDF p. 360)
questions.quote: Excessive urine output indicates diabetes insipidus.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A head-injury client has bruising behind the ear and around both eyes. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Battle's sign and raccoon eyes indicate basilar skull fracture; watch for CSF otorrhea or rhinorrhea.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Head trauma (PDF p. 361)
questions.quote: Battle's sign (hematoma at the mastoid process/ behind the ear). Raccoon eyes (periorbital ecchymosis)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Bloody fluid from a head-injury client's nose forms a yellow ring around a blood spot on gauze. This indicates:
questions.rationale: A positive halo (ring) sign suggests CSF; CSF is also positive for glucose.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Head trauma (PDF p. 361)
questions.quote: yellowish ring encircles the blood if CSF is present

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which tremor is typical of Parkinson's disease?
questions.rationale: Parkinson's causes resting (non-intention) pill-rolling tremor that worsens at rest.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Parkinson's disease (PDF p. 361)
questions.quote: The initial sign is tremors - pill rolling tremors

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Parkinson's disease walks with short, accelerating steps and cannot stop easily. This is:
questions.rationale: Shuffling, festinating gait speeds up and is hard to stop; there is no true paralysis or sensory loss.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Parkinson's disease (PDF p. 362)
questions.quote: lhe chamcteristic gait of the client is shuffling, festinating gait.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on benztropine reports dry mouth. The nurse suggests:
questions.rationale: Anticholinergics cause dry mouth, urinary retention and constipation; relieve with sugarless gum or ice chips.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Anticholinergics (PDF p. 363)
questions.quote: Relieve dry mouth with hard candy, ice chips or sugarless chewing gum.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Anticholinergic drugs for Parkinson's disease are avoided in clients with:
questions.rationale: Anticholinergics can raise intraocular pressure and are avoided in glaucoma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Anticholinergics (PDF p. 363)
questions.quote: Clients who have glaucoma should not take anticholinergics.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Carbidopa is combined with levodopa because carbidopa:
options: Lets more levodopa reach the brain
Crosses into the brain as dopamine
questions.rationale: Carbidopa blocks peripheral breakdown of levodopa so more reaches the brain at lower doses.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Dopaminergics (PDF p. 363)
questions.quote: Carbidopa reduces destruction of levodopa at the periphery.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client starting carbidopa-levodopa should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Orthostatic hypotension is common; darkened urine and sweat are harmless. MAOIs cause hypertensive crisis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Carbidopa-levodopa therapy (PDF p. 363)
questions.quote: Advise client to practice gradual change of position to prevent orthostatic hypotension.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Muscle weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest is typical of:
questions.rationale: MG impairs neuromuscular transmission; weakness (ptosis, diplopia, dysphagia) worsens with activity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Myasthenia gravis (PDF p. 365)
questions.quote: Muscle weakness associated with activity relieved by rest

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis missed two doses and now has severe respiratory distress, cyanosis and an absent cough reflex. This is most likely:
questions.rationale: Myasthenic crisis is caused by undermedication; it can need more cholinergic drug and mechanical ventilation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Myasthenic crisis (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: Myasthenic crisis is caused by undermedication.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with MG has increased salivation, sweating, small pupils and weakness after a dose increase. This is:
questions.rationale: Cholinergic crisis from overdose: salivation, sweating, miosis, cramps, weakness; atropine is the antidote.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Cholinergic crisis (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: Cholinergic crisis is caused by excessive medications.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug should be at the bedside for cholinergic crisis?
questions.rationale: Atropine counteracts excess cholinergic effects.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (PDF p. 366)
questions.quote: Have readily available an antidote for cholinergic crisis (Atropine Sulfate).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which antibiotic may worsen weakness in myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Neomycin (aminoglycoside), muscle relaxants, morphine and barbiturates worsen myoneural transmission.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 MG drugs to avoid (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: • Neomycin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with multiple sclerosis should avoid:
questions.rationale: Heat worsens weakness in MS; exacerbations are triggered by fatigue, chilling and stress.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Multiple sclerosis (PDF p. 368)
questions.quote: Avoid hot baths. Heat increases weakness.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Scanning speech, intention tremor and nystagmus form Charcot's triad of:
questions.rationale: Charcot's triad is classic for MS (demyelination of CNS).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Multiple sclerosis (PDF p. 368)
questions.quote: S - canning speech I - ntention tremors N ystagmus

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: In early Alzheimer's disease, which memory is lost first?
questions.rationale: Recent memory fails first; remote memory may remain for a long time, so reminiscence helps.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Alzheimer's disease (PDF p. 369)
questions.quote: Loss of recent memory occurs first. Remote memory may remain intact for a long period of time.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with Alzheimer's becomes agitated each evening. Which helps?
questions.rationale: Prevent sundowning: lights on before dusk, routine, calm approach; avoid hypnotics and arguing.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Alzheimer's disease (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: Turn lights on before it becomes dark.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How should the nurse give instructions to a client with dementia?
questions.rationale: Ask one question and give one direction at a time; call the client by name; allow time.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Alzheimer's disease (PDF p. 370)
questions.quote: Ask only one question at a time and give one direction at a time.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ascending paralysis after a recent viral illness, with risk to breathing, suggests:
questions.rationale: GBS is autoimmune demyelination with ascending paralysis; monitor respiratory function closely.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Guillain-Barré syndrome (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: Ascending or descending paralysis which may progress to respiratory muscle paralysis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which recent history is most often reported by a client newly diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome?
questions.rationale: GBS is autoimmune demyelination usually preceded by a mild respiratory or GI infection.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Guillain-Barré syndrome (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: It is usually preceded by mild upper respiratory infection or gastroenteritis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with trigeminal neuralgia should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Avoid triggers (hot/cold foods, wind, chewing on the affected side); carbamazepine is often used.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Trigeminal neuralgia (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: Instruct client to chew food on the unaffected side.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Bell's palsy cannot fully close one eye. The nurse should:
options: Apply hot packs to the eye
questions.rationale: Protect the eye (lubricant, patch at night) to prevent corneal injury; encourage facial exercises.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Bell's palsy (PDF p. 373)
questions.quote: Protect the eyes from dryness and prevent injury.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: At the scene of a diving accident with suspected neck injury, the first priority is:
questions.rationale: Ensure airway and breathing while immobilizing the spine; transport as a unit and never realign body parts.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Spinal cord injury (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: First priority: promotion of respiratory function especially in cervical SCI.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A spinal cord injury client has flaccid paralysis, absent reflexes, hypotension and bradycardia soon after injury. This is:
questions.rationale: Spinal shock causes flaccid paralysis and areflexia below the lesion, with hypotension and bradycardia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Spinal shock (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: It is a period of flaccid paralysis and a complete loss of all reflexes occurs.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with a C6 injury suddenly has severe headache, BP 200/110 and sweating above the lesion. The nurse first:
questions.rationale: Autonomic dysreflexia: raise the head to lower BP and find the trigger, most often a distended bladder or impaction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Autonomic dysreflexia (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: Place the client in sitting position. To lower BP by gravity. o Check bladder distention.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Autonomic dysreflexia occurs mainly in spinal injuries at or above:
questions.rationale: Lesions at or above T6, especially cervical, allow uncontrolled sympathetic reflexes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Autonomic dysreflexia (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: It occurs in clients with SCI above Tc, most often in cervical injuries.
